definition: The party who initiates a lawsuit by filing a complaint, seeking a legal remedy against the defendant.
plainEnglish: The person doing the suing.

definition: The party against whom a lawsuit is brought and who must respond to the plaintiff's allegations.
plainEnglish: The person being sued (or charged, in a criminal case).

definition: The initial pleading filed by a plaintiff that states the basis for the lawsuit, the legal claims, and the relief sought.
plainEnglish: The document that starts a lawsuit, explaining what happened and what the plaintiff wants.

definition: The defendant's formal written response to the complaint, admitting or denying each allegation and raising any affirmative defenses.
plainEnglish: The defendant's official reply to the lawsuit.

definition: A formal request made to the court asking for a specific ruling or order, either before, during, or after trial.
plainEnglish: An ask to the judge for something.

definition: A request asking the court to throw out a case on legal grounds before reaching the merits, often for failure to state a claim or lack of jurisdiction.
plainEnglish: A request to throw out the case because it's legally defective.

definition: A judgment entered without a full trial when there is no genuine dispute over any material fact and one party is entitled to judgment as a matter of law.
plainEnglish: Winning (or losing) the case before trial because the facts aren't really in dispute.
synonyms: judgment as a matter of law

definition: The pretrial process by which parties exchange information and evidence relevant to the case through depositions, interrogatories, document requests, and admissions.
plainEnglish: The phase before trial where each side digs up information from the other.

definition: Sworn out-of-court testimony of a witness, taken under oath and recorded for use in pretrial discovery or at trial.
plainEnglish: An interview under oath, recorded by a court reporter, used to lock in a witness's story.

definition: A written question served by one party on another that must be answered in writing and under oath as part of discovery.
plainEnglish: A written question the other side has to answer in writing.

definition: A formal court order requiring a person to appear and give testimony (subpoena ad testificandum) or produce documents (subpoena duces tecum).
plainEnglish: A court order making someone show up to testify or hand over documents.

definition: A formal notice to a defendant that a lawsuit has been filed and that they must appear in court or respond by a certain date.
plainEnglish: The official notice that someone is being sued.

definition: The formal delivery of legal documents (such as a summons and complaint) to a party to give them notice of legal proceedings.
plainEnglish: Officially handing the lawsuit papers to the defendant.

definition: The authority of a court to hear and decide a case, including authority over the subject matter and the parties.
plainEnglish: Whether this particular court is allowed to hear this case.

definition: A court's power over the parties in a case, generally requiring minimum contacts between the defendant and the forum state.
plainEnglish: Whether the court has authority over this particular defendant.

definition: A court's power to hear a particular type of case, such as federal question or diversity jurisdiction in federal court.
plainEnglish: Whether this kind of case belongs in this type of court at all.

definition: The proper geographic location for trying a case, typically based on where parties reside or where events occurred.
plainEnglish: Which courthouse (geographically) is the right place to try the case.

definition: The legal right to bring a lawsuit, requiring an injury in fact, causation, and redressability.
plainEnglish: Whether this person is the right party to be bringing this lawsuit.

definition: A lawsuit in which one or more plaintiffs sue on behalf of a larger group of similarly situated people.
plainEnglish: One lawsuit brought by a few people on behalf of many.

definition: A claim brought by a defendant against a plaintiff in the same lawsuit, asserting that the plaintiff is liable to the defendant.
plainEnglish: The defendant's own lawsuit against the plaintiff, filed inside the same case.

definition: A claim brought by one party against a co-party (e.g., one defendant against another defendant) in the same lawsuit.
plainEnglish: When co-defendants (or co-plaintiffs) sue each other within the same case.

definition: The process of questioning prospective jurors to determine their suitability and uncover potential bias.
plainEnglish: Questioning potential jurors to pick the jury.

definition: A party's right to dismiss a potential juror without stating a reason, limited in number and subject to anti-discrimination rules.
plainEnglish: Striking a juror without having to explain why.

definition: A request to remove a prospective juror based on a specific reason such as bias or inability to be impartial.
plainEnglish: Striking a juror with a stated, valid reason.

definition: The formal decision of a jury (or judge in a bench trial) on the issues of fact submitted to it.
plainEnglish: The jury's (or judge's) final decision in the case.

definition: The official decision of a court resolving a dispute and determining the rights and obligations of the parties.
plainEnglish: The court's final ruling that ends the case.

definition: A request to a higher court to review and change the decision of a lower court.
plainEnglish: Asking a higher court to overturn the lower court's ruling.

definition: A standard of appellate review in which the higher court considers the matter anew, without deference to the lower court's conclusions on issues of law.
plainEnglish: The appeals court looks at it fresh, without giving weight to what the trial court decided.

definition: A standard of appellate review requiring the appellant to show that the lower court's decision was arbitrary, unreasonable, or based on an erroneous view of the law.
plainEnglish: Reversing a trial judge only if they got it really wrong, not just because the appeals court would have decided differently.

definition: The doctrine that a final judgment on the merits by a competent court bars the same parties from relitigating the same claim.
plainEnglish: You can't sue over the same thing twice once it's been decided.

definition: The doctrine that prevents a party from relitigating an issue of fact or law that was actually litigated and necessarily decided in a prior action.
plainEnglish: You can't re-fight a specific issue that's already been decided in an earlier case.

definition: The doctrine that courts should follow precedent and not disturb settled matters, promoting consistency and predictability in the law.
plainEnglish: Courts follow what earlier courts decided.

definition: Representing oneself in court without an attorney.
plainEnglish: Acting as your own lawyer.

definition: A 'friend of the court'—a non-party who, with leave of court, files a brief offering information or argument relevant to the case.
plainEnglish: An outsider, usually an organization, who weighs in on a case they're not actually a party to.

definition: A proceeding held in private, typically in the judge's chambers, outside the presence of the jury or public.
plainEnglish: Done privately, in the judge's chambers.

definition: An action or communication involving only one party, without notice to or argument from the other side.
plainEnglish: Done with only one side present.

definition: A doctrine allowing a court to decline jurisdiction when another forum would be more convenient and just for the parties.
plainEnglish: When the court says 'this case really belongs somewhere else more convenient.'

definition: The transfer of a case from state court to federal court when the case could have originally been filed in federal court.
plainEnglish: Moving a state-court case to federal court.

definition: Sending a case back to a lower court for further proceedings, or returning a removed case to state court.
plainEnglish: Sending the case back—either to the trial court after appeal, or to state court after removal.

definition: A civil wrong, other than breach of contract, for which the law provides a remedy in the form of damages.
plainEnglish: A wrongful act (not a contract violation) that lets the injured person sue.

definition: Failure to exercise the standard of care that a reasonably prudent person would exercise under similar circumstances, resulting in harm.
plainEnglish: Carelessness that causes injury.

definition: A legal obligation owed by one person to another, breach of which can give rise to liability in tort.
plainEnglish: A legal obligation you owe to someone else (like to drive carefully).

definition: Failure to meet a legal duty or obligation, whether in tort (breach of duty of care) or contract (breach of promise).
plainEnglish: Failing to do what you were legally required to do.

definition: The causal link between a defendant's conduct and the plaintiff's harm, generally requiring both actual cause and proximate cause.
plainEnglish: Proving the defendant's conduct actually caused the harm.

definition: A legal limitation on liability requiring that the harm be a reasonably foreseeable consequence of the defendant's conduct.
plainEnglish: The cause has to be close enough and foreseeable enough that it's fair to hold the defendant responsible.

definition: Actual cause—the harm would not have occurred but for the defendant's conduct.
plainEnglish: If the defendant hadn't done it, this harm wouldn't have happened.

definition: Monetary compensation awarded to a party who has suffered harm or loss due to another's wrongful act.
plainEnglish: Money the wrongdoer has to pay the injured party.

definition: Damages awarded to make the injured party whole by reimbursing actual losses, including economic and non-economic harm.
plainEnglish: Money meant to put the victim back where they would have been.

definition: Damages awarded above and beyond compensation to punish the defendant for outrageous conduct and deter similar future conduct.
plainEnglish: Extra money meant to punish the defendant and warn off others.

definition: A small sum awarded when a legal right has been violated but no actual loss has been proven.
plainEnglish: A token amount (like $1) recognizing a wrong even though there's no real loss.

definition: Liability imposed without regard to fault, typically for abnormally dangerous activities or defective products.
plainEnglish: You're liable even if you weren't careless—just because you did the thing.

definition: The liability of manufacturers and sellers for injuries caused by defective products, typically based on negligence, strict liability, or breach of warranty.
plainEnglish: Holding companies responsible when their defective products hurt people.

definition: An intentional, harmful or offensive contact with another person without their consent.
plainEnglish: Intentionally touching someone in a harmful or offensive way without permission.

definition: An intentional act that causes another person to reasonably apprehend imminent harmful or offensive contact.
plainEnglish: Making someone reasonably fear they're about to be physically hurt.

definition: The intentional and unlawful restraint of a person's freedom of movement without legal justification.
plainEnglish: Holding someone against their will without legal right.

definition: Tort liability for extreme and outrageous conduct intentionally or recklessly causing severe emotional distress to another.
plainEnglish: Doing something so outrageous to someone that it causes serious emotional trauma.

definition: A false statement of fact communicated to a third party that damages the reputation of the subject.
plainEnglish: Saying or writing something false that damages someone's reputation.

definition: Defamation in a written or recorded form.
plainEnglish: Defamation in writing.

definition: Defamation in an oral or spoken form.
plainEnglish: Defamation spoken out loud.

definition: A doctrine permitting an inference of negligence from the very nature of an accident, where the cause is exclusively within the defendant's control and the accident would not ordinarily occur without negligence.
plainEnglish: Latin for 'the thing speaks for itself'—the accident itself shows someone was negligent.

definition: A doctrine that reduces a plaintiff's damages in proportion to their own degree of fault in causing the injury.
plainEnglish: Plaintiff's recovery is reduced based on how much they were at fault too.

definition: A common-law doctrine, now largely replaced by comparative negligence, that bars a plaintiff from recovery if they were even slightly at fault.
plainEnglish: Old rule—if the plaintiff was at all to blame, they get nothing.

definition: A defense barring recovery when the plaintiff knowingly and voluntarily accepted a known risk that caused the injury.
plainEnglish: You knew it was dangerous and did it anyway, so you can't sue.

definition: Liability imposed on one person for the wrongful acts of another based on the relationship between them, such as employer-employee.
plainEnglish: Being held responsible for someone else's wrongdoing because of your relationship to them.

definition: The doctrine that an employer is liable for the wrongful acts of an employee committed within the scope of employment.
plainEnglish: Latin for 'let the master answer'—employers are on the hook for what their employees do on the job.

definition: A doctrine allowing the plaintiff to collect the entire judgment from any one of multiple tortfeasors, who must then seek contribution from others.
plainEnglish: When multiple defendants are liable, the plaintiff can collect the full amount from any one of them.

definition: A legally enforceable agreement between two or more parties, typically requiring offer, acceptance, consideration, and mutual assent.
plainEnglish: A legally binding deal.

definition: A manifestation of willingness to enter into a bargain, justifying another person in understanding that their assent will conclude the agreement.
plainEnglish: A proposal to make a deal that the other side can accept.

definition: A manifestation of assent to the terms of an offer, made in the manner invited or required by the offer.
plainEnglish: Saying yes to a deal in the way the offer required.

definition: Something of value (an act, forbearance, or promise) bargained for and given in exchange for a promise, required to make a contract enforceable.
plainEnglish: The 'something for something'—each side has to give up or do something for the deal to count.

definition: The agreement of all parties to a contract on the same terms, traditionally called a 'meeting of the minds.'
plainEnglish: Both sides actually agreed to the same deal.

definition: A doctrine requiring certain contracts (such as those involving land, marriage, or performance over a year) to be in writing and signed to be enforceable.
plainEnglish: Some kinds of contracts have to be in writing or they can't be enforced.

definition: A doctrine excluding prior or contemporaneous oral or written statements that contradict or vary the terms of a fully integrated written contract.
plainEnglish: Once you sign a final written contract, you can't bring in earlier promises to change it.

definition: A doctrine enforcing a promise lacking consideration when the promisor reasonably should have expected reliance and injustice can be avoided only by enforcement.
plainEnglish: Enforcing a promise (even without a formal contract) because someone reasonably relied on it.

definition: A defense to contract enforcement where the terms are so unfair and one-sided that no reasonable person would agree to them, often combining procedural and substantive elements.
plainEnglish: The contract is so unfair that the court refuses to enforce it.

definition: An unlawful threat or coercion that overcomes a person's free will, making a contract voidable.
plainEnglish: Forcing someone to sign a contract by threatening them.

definition: An equitable remedy ordering a party to perform their contractual obligation, typically granted when damages are inadequate, such as in unique-goods or real estate contracts.
plainEnglish: The court orders the breaching party to actually do what they promised, not just pay money.

definition: Damages whose amount has been agreed upon in the contract itself, enforceable if reasonable and not a penalty.
plainEnglish: A pre-agreed dollar amount written into the contract for if someone breaches.

definition: Damages designed to put the non-breaching party in the position they would have been in if the contract had been performed.
plainEnglish: Money meant to give you what you would have had if the deal had gone through.

definition: The duty of a non-breaching party to take reasonable steps to reduce the damages caused by the breach.
plainEnglish: After a breach, you have to try to limit your own losses.

definition: A clear and unequivocal indication by one party, before performance is due, that they will not perform the contract.
plainEnglish: Telling the other side in advance that you won't be keeping your end of the deal.

definition: A breach so significant that it defeats the essential purpose of the contract and excuses the non-breaching party from further performance.
plainEnglish: A breach big enough that the other side can walk away from the contract.

definition: A contract clause excusing performance due to extraordinary events beyond the parties' control, such as natural disasters, war, or pandemics.
plainEnglish: An 'act of God' clause that excuses performance when something massive and unforeseen happens.

definition: A contractual obligation by one party to compensate another for specified losses or liabilities.
plainEnglish: A promise to cover the other party's losses if certain bad things happen.

definition: A promise or assurance, express or implied, that certain facts or conditions are true or will happen.
plainEnglish: A guarantee built into a contract.

definition: The substitution of a new contract or new party in place of an existing one, with the consent of all parties, discharging the original obligation.
plainEnglish: Swapping out the old contract (or an old party) for a new one, with everyone's agreement.

definition: The transfer of contractual rights from one party (assignor) to a third party (assignee).
plainEnglish: Handing off your right to receive something under a contract to someone else.

definition: The transfer of contractual duties to a third party, though the delegating party generally remains liable for performance.
plainEnglish: Handing off your duties under a contract to someone else (though you're still on the hook).

definition: A person who, although not a party to a contract, was intended to benefit from it and may enforce it.
plainEnglish: Someone who isn't in the contract but is meant to benefit from it and can sue to enforce it.

definition: A serious crime, typically punishable by imprisonment for more than one year or by death.
plainEnglish: A serious crime, generally one that can land you in prison for over a year.

definition: A less serious crime, typically punishable by a fine or imprisonment of one year or less.
plainEnglish: A less serious crime, usually punishable by less than a year in jail.

definition: The mental state or intent required to commit a particular crime; literally 'guilty mind.'
plainEnglish: The 'guilty mind'—whether the person intended (or was reckless about) the crime.

definition: The physical act or unlawful conduct required to constitute a crime; literally 'guilty act.'
plainEnglish: The 'guilty act'—the physical thing the person did.

definition: A reasonable basis, based on facts and circumstances, to believe a crime has been or is being committed; the standard for arrests and search warrants.
plainEnglish: Enough reason to believe a crime happened to justify an arrest or search.

definition: A standard lower than probable cause, requiring specific and articulable facts suggesting criminal activity; sufficient for a brief investigative stop.
plainEnglish: Enough to briefly stop and question someone, but not enough to arrest them.

definition: The highest standard of proof, required to convict in criminal cases; doubt based on reason after considering all the evidence.
plainEnglish: The high bar prosecutors have to clear to convict—no reasonable doubt that the defendant did it.

definition: The standard of proof in most civil cases, meaning more likely than not (greater than 50%).
plainEnglish: More likely true than not—the bar in most civil cases.

definition: An intermediate standard of proof requiring a high probability of truth, used in certain civil matters such as fraud, termination of parental rights, and punitive damages.
plainEnglish: Higher than 'more likely than not' but lower than 'beyond a reasonable doubt.'

definition: Warnings required to be given by police to suspects in custody before interrogation, advising them of their rights to remain silent and to counsel.
plainEnglish: The 'you have the right to remain silent' warning before police questioning.

definition: A rule prohibiting the use at trial of evidence obtained in violation of the defendant's constitutional rights.
plainEnglish: Evidence cops got illegally can't be used at trial.

definition: A doctrine excluding evidence derived from an illegal search, arrest, or interrogation, including evidence obtained indirectly.
plainEnglish: Evidence that came from an illegal search is also tainted and excluded.

definition: The Fifth Amendment protection against being tried twice for the same offense by the same sovereign.
plainEnglish: You can't be tried twice for the same crime in the same jurisdiction.

definition: A writ requiring a person under detention to be brought before a court to determine whether their imprisonment is lawful.
plainEnglish: A challenge that says 'the government is holding me illegally—prove it has the right to.'

definition: A negotiated agreement in which a defendant pleads guilty to a charge in exchange for some concession by the prosecution, such as reduced charges or a lighter sentence.
plainEnglish: A deal where the defendant pleads guilty in exchange for a lighter charge or sentence.

definition: A formal written accusation by a grand jury charging a person with a crime.
plainEnglish: A grand jury's formal charging document accusing someone of a crime.

definition: A court proceeding where a defendant is formally charged, informed of the charges, and asked to enter a plea.
plainEnglish: The first court appearance where the defendant hears the charges and enters a plea.

definition: Money or property pledged to the court to secure a defendant's release from custody and ensure their appearance at trial.
plainEnglish: Money or property put up to get out of jail before trial, forfeited if the defendant skips court.

definition: A defense justifying the use of force to protect oneself from imminent unlawful harm, generally requiring proportional response.
plainEnglish: The defense that you used force because you were defending yourself from an attack.

definition: A defense asserting that the defendant should not be held criminally responsible because, at the time of the offense, a mental disease or defect prevented them from understanding the nature of their act or that it was wrong.
plainEnglish: A defense that the defendant was so mentally ill they couldn't be held responsible.

definition: The most complete form of ownership in real property, lasting indefinitely and freely transferable.
plainEnglish: Full ownership of land with no time limit—you own it outright.

definition: An interest in real property limited in duration to the life of a specified person.
plainEnglish: You own and use the property only during your (or someone else's) lifetime.

definition: A nonpossessory right to use another's land for a specific purpose, such as a right of way.
plainEnglish: A legal right to use part of someone else's land for a specific purpose.

definition: The acquisition of title to land by openly occupying it for a statutory period in a manner hostile to the true owner's rights.
plainEnglish: Gaining ownership of land by using it openly and without permission long enough.

definition: The government's power to take private property for public use, subject to payment of just compensation.
plainEnglish: The government's power to take private property for public use (paying fair value for it).

definition: Co-ownership of property in equal shares with a right of survivorship—when one tenant dies, their interest passes automatically to the survivors.
plainEnglish: Co-ownership where if one owner dies, their share automatically goes to the others.

definition: Co-ownership where each owner has a separate, undivided interest that can be sold or inherited, with no right of survivorship.
plainEnglish: Co-ownership where each person can leave their share to whoever they want when they die.

definition: A security interest in real property given by a borrower to a lender to secure repayment of a loan.
plainEnglish: Using your house as collateral for a loan.

definition: A legal document transferring ownership of real property from one party to another.
plainEnglish: The legal document that transfers ownership of real estate.

definition: Legal ownership of property and the evidence of that ownership.
plainEnglish: Legal ownership of property.

definition: A buyer who acquires property in good faith, for value, and without notice of competing claims, often gaining superior title.
plainEnglish: Someone who buys property in good faith, paying real money, without knowing about any other claims to it.

definition: An out-of-court statement offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted, generally inadmissible unless an exception applies.
plainEnglish: Repeating what someone else said outside of court, to prove it's true—generally not allowed.

definition: Evidence is relevant if it has any tendency to make a fact of consequence more or less probable than it would be without the evidence.
plainEnglish: Whether the evidence has anything to do with the issues in the case.

definition: The degree to which a piece of evidence makes a fact more or less probable, weighed against potential unfair prejudice.
plainEnglish: How much the evidence actually helps prove (or disprove) something.

definition: A privilege protecting confidential communications between a lawyer and client made for the purpose of obtaining legal advice.
plainEnglish: Things you say to your lawyer in confidence can't be used against you.

definition: A doctrine protecting materials prepared by or for an attorney in anticipation of litigation from discovery by opposing counsel.
plainEnglish: Your lawyer's notes, strategies, and prep materials are generally shielded from the other side.

definition: A rule requiring the original document (or a reliable duplicate) to prove its contents, rather than testimony about the document.
plainEnglish: If you want to prove what a document says, you generally have to produce the document itself.

definition: Evidence of a person's character or character trait, generally inadmissible to prove conduct on a particular occasion but admissible for other purposes.
plainEnglish: Evidence about someone's general character (good or bad), usually not allowed to prove they did something.

definition: A witness qualified by knowledge, skill, experience, training, or education to offer opinion testimony on matters beyond lay understanding.
plainEnglish: A specialist allowed to give expert opinions in court.

definition: The federal standard for admissibility of expert testimony, requiring the trial judge to determine whether the expert's methodology is scientifically reliable and relevant.
plainEnglish: Federal courts' test for whether an expert's methods are reliable enough to testify.

definition: A hearsay exception allowing statements made under the stress of a startling event, while the declarant remains under that stress.
plainEnglish: Something said in the heat of a shocking moment—an exception to the hearsay rule.

definition: A hearsay exception for statements made by a declarant who believes death is imminent, concerning the cause or circumstances of impending death.
plainEnglish: What someone says when they think they're dying—admissible despite hearsay rules.

definition: Court recognition of a fact as true without requiring proof, generally limited to facts that are commonly known or readily verifiable.
plainEnglish: When the court accepts a well-known fact as true without anyone having to prove it.

definition: The constitutional guarantee that the government will not deprive a person of life, liberty, or property without fair procedures and substantive fairness.
plainEnglish: The government has to play fair before taking your life, freedom, or property.

definition: The constitutional requirement of fair procedures—generally notice and an opportunity to be heard—before government deprives someone of life, liberty, or property.
plainEnglish: Notice and a chance to be heard before the government takes something from you.

definition: The constitutional doctrine protecting fundamental rights from government interference, regardless of the procedures used.
plainEnglish: Some rights are so fundamental that no fair procedure can justify taking them away.

definition: The Fourteenth Amendment guarantee that the government will not deny any person within its jurisdiction the equal protection of the laws.
plainEnglish: The government has to treat similarly situated people similarly.

definition: The most rigorous standard of judicial review, requiring laws to be narrowly tailored to serve a compelling government interest. Applied to suspect classifications and fundamental rights.
plainEnglish: The toughest level of constitutional review—laws almost always fail it.

definition: A middle-tier standard of review requiring laws to be substantially related to an important government interest, applied to classifications like gender.
plainEnglish: A middle-level constitutional test, used for things like gender classifications.

definition: The most deferential standard of review, requiring only that a law be rationally related to a legitimate government interest. Most laws survive this test.
plainEnglish: The easy-pass constitutional test—any half-decent reason will do.

definition: The constitutional provision (Article I, § 8) granting Congress the power to regulate commerce with foreign nations, among the states, and with Indian tribes.
plainEnglish: The part of the Constitution that gives Congress power to regulate business and commerce.

definition: The constitutional amendment protecting freedoms of religion, speech, press, peaceful assembly, and the right to petition the government.
plainEnglish: The free speech, religion, press, assembly, and petition amendment.

definition: The First Amendment clause prohibiting government establishment of religion, generally requiring separation between church and state.
plainEnglish: The government can't establish or favor a religion.

definition: The First Amendment clause protecting the right to practice one's religion without undue government interference.
plainEnglish: The government can't stop you from practicing your religion.

definition: A legal entity created under state law that is separate from its owners (shareholders) and has rights and obligations distinct from those of the individuals who form it.
plainEnglish: A business treated by the law as its own 'person,' separate from the people who own it.

definition: A hybrid business entity offering limited liability protection like a corporation while allowing pass-through taxation and flexible management like a partnership.
plainEnglish: A flexible business structure that protects owners from personal liability and is taxed like a partnership.

definition: A judicial doctrine allowing courts to hold shareholders personally liable for corporate obligations when the corporation is used to perpetrate fraud or is a mere alter ego of its owners.
plainEnglish: When the court goes after the people behind a sham corporation personally.

definition: A legal duty to act in the best interests of another party, typically involving duties of loyalty, care, and good faith.
plainEnglish: A duty to put someone else's interests ahead of your own.

definition: A presumption that corporate directors acted on an informed basis, in good faith, and in the honest belief their actions were in the company's best interest.
plainEnglish: Courts give corporate directors the benefit of the doubt on business decisions made in good faith.

definition: A legal document expressing how a person wants their property distributed after death, typically requiring formalities such as writing, signature, and witnesses.
plainEnglish: The legal document saying who gets your stuff when you die.

definition: A person who makes a will.
plainEnglish: The person whose will it is (testatrix if female, in older usage).

definition: The condition of dying without a valid will, in which case property passes according to state intestacy laws.
plainEnglish: Dying without a will.

definition: The court-supervised process of validating a will, administering an estate, and distributing assets to heirs and beneficiaries.
plainEnglish: The court process for sorting out someone's estate after they die.

definition: A legal arrangement where one party (trustee) holds and manages property for the benefit of another (beneficiary), created by a grantor or settlor.
plainEnglish: An arrangement where someone holds and manages property for the benefit of someone else.

definition: A legal document authorizing one person (the agent or attorney-in-fact) to act on behalf of another (the principal) in specified matters.
plainEnglish: A document letting someone else act legally on your behalf.

definition: Sufficient on its face; a prima facie case is one with enough evidence to proceed unless rebutted.
plainEnglish: 'On its face'—at first glance, enough evidence to make the case.

definition: Something for something; an exchange of equivalent value.
plainEnglish: 'This for that'—an exchange where each side gives the other something.

definition: In the place of a parent; describing someone, often a school or guardian, who has assumed parental duties.
plainEnglish: 'In the place of a parent'—standing in for a parent legally.

definition: Let the buyer beware—the principle that buyers must inspect goods and bear the risk of defects unless protected by warranty or statute.
plainEnglish: 'Let the buyer beware'—you bought it, you live with it.

definition: In fact, as a matter of practice, regardless of official status; often contrasted with de jure.
plainEnglish: 'In reality'—what's actually happening, even if it's not official.

definition: By law, as a matter of legal right; often contrasted with de facto.
plainEnglish: 'By law'—what the law officially says, even if reality differs.

definition: Of its own kind; unique and not fitting into established categories.
plainEnglish: 'One of a kind'—doesn't fit any existing category.

definition: For this purpose; created for a specific, immediate need rather than general application.
plainEnglish: 'For this'—made for one specific situation.

definition: For the purposes of the lawsuit; a guardian ad litem, for instance, is appointed to represent a party only for the duration of a case.
plainEnglish: 'For the lawsuit'—appointed only for this case.

definition: Of its own accord; describing an action taken by a court on its own initiative without a motion or request.
plainEnglish: 'On its own'—when the judge does something without anyone asking.

definition: Now for then; describing a court action with retroactive effect, as if it had been done at an earlier date.
plainEnglish: 'Now for then'—backdating a court order to fix an earlier omission.

definition: Without which not; an essential condition or indispensable element.
plainEnglish: 'Without which, nothing'—an absolutely essential element.

definition: Beyond the powers; an act outside the legal authority of a corporation, officer, or government entity.
plainEnglish: 'Beyond the powers'—doing something you weren't legally allowed to do.

definition: In good faith; genuine, sincere, and without intent to deceive.
plainEnglish: 'In good faith'—legitimate and honest.

definition: Wrong in itself; conduct that is inherently immoral or wrongful, such as murder or theft.
plainEnglish: 'Wrong in itself'—things everyone agrees are evil, like murder.

definition: Wrong because prohibited; conduct that is wrongful only because a statute makes it so, such as traffic violations.
plainEnglish: 'Wrong because banned'—only illegal because there's a law against it.

definition: Among other things; used when citing a few examples from a larger group.
plainEnglish: 'Among other things.'

definition: Against the person; describing an action or jurisdiction directed at a specific person rather than property.
plainEnglish: 'Against the person'—a case directed at a particular individual.

definition: Against the thing; describing an action directed at property itself rather than a particular person.
plainEnglish: 'Against the thing'—a case directed at a piece of property, not a person.

definition: For the public good; legal services provided without charge, typically for clients who cannot afford counsel.
plainEnglish: Legal work done for free.

definition: At the threshold; a motion in limine asks the court to rule on the admissibility of evidence before it is offered at trial.
plainEnglish: A pretrial motion to keep certain evidence out of trial.

definition: With even stronger reason; used in legal argument to indicate that a conclusion follows even more strongly from a stronger premise.
plainEnglish: 'Even more so'—if X is true, then Y is even more obviously true.

definition: And the following; used in citations to indicate that the cited section continues with subsequent sections.
plainEnglish: 'And what follows'—citation shorthand meaning the cited section plus the ones after.

definition: And others; used in case captions and citations to indicate additional parties or authors beyond those named.
plainEnglish: 'And others'—shorthand for additional parties or authors.

definition: A liquidation bankruptcy under the U.S. Bankruptcy Code in which a trustee gathers and sells the debtor's nonexempt property to pay creditors.
plainEnglish: 'Wipe-out' bankruptcy—non-exempt assets are sold off and most debts are discharged.

definition: A reorganization bankruptcy, typically used by businesses, allowing the debtor to continue operating while restructuring debts under court supervision.
plainEnglish: Business reorganization bankruptcy—the company keeps running while it restructures its debts.

definition: A consumer bankruptcy reorganization allowing individuals with regular income to repay debts over three to five years under a court-approved plan.
plainEnglish: Individual repayment-plan bankruptcy—you keep your stuff but pay off debts over 3-5 years.

definition: An injunction that automatically takes effect upon filing a bankruptcy petition, halting most collection efforts and lawsuits against the debtor.
plainEnglish: An instant freeze on collection efforts the moment someone files for bankruptcy.

definition: A court order in bankruptcy releasing the debtor from personal liability for most pre-petition debts.
plainEnglish: The bankruptcy court wiping out your debts.

definition: A parent's legal authority and responsibility regarding the care, control, and decision-making for a child, split between legal custody and physical custody.
plainEnglish: Who has the right to make decisions for and live with a child.

definition: Court-ordered financial support paid by one ex-spouse to the other after a divorce or separation.
plainEnglish: Spousal support paid after divorce.

definition: Court-ordered payments made by a non-custodial parent to the custodial parent for the support of their child.
plainEnglish: Payments by one parent to the other for the kids' expenses.

definition: The legal standard guiding decisions in child custody, visitation, and adoption matters, focused on the child's welfare rather than the parents' preferences.
plainEnglish: The rule that says decisions about kids should put the kid's well-being first.

definition: A contract entered into before marriage that establishes how assets and debts will be divided in the event of divorce or death.
plainEnglish: A 'prenup'—a deal made before marriage about who gets what if it ends.

definition: A defense that, even if the plaintiff's allegations are true, defeats or mitigates the claim, such as statute of limitations or self-defense.
plainEnglish: 'Even if everything you say is true, I still win because of X.'

definition: A law setting the maximum time after an event within which a lawsuit may be filed.
plainEnglish: The deadline for filing a lawsuit.

definition: The legal suspension or pausing of a statute of limitations, preventing the time from running during the tolled period.
plainEnglish: Pausing the clock on the statute of limitations.

definition: The obligation of a party to prove disputed facts to a specified level of certainty, encompassing both the burden of production and the burden of persuasion.
plainEnglish: Whose job it is to prove what, and how convincingly.

definition: A court order requiring a party to do or refrain from doing specific acts; may be temporary, preliminary, or permanent.
plainEnglish: A court order making someone do—or stop doing—something.

definition: An emergency, short-term injunction issued without full hearing to prevent immediate, irreparable harm pending a fuller hearing on a preliminary injunction.
plainEnglish: An emergency, short-term court order to prevent immediate harm.

definition: An injunction issued before trial to preserve the status quo, requiring the moving party to show likelihood of success, irreparable harm, and balance of equities in their favor.
plainEnglish: A court order issued early in a case to hold things in place until trial.

definition: The mental state required for certain crimes where the defendant must intend a specific further consequence beyond the act itself, such as intent to permanently deprive in larceny.
plainEnglish: Intending not just the act, but a specific further outcome.

definition: The mental state required for crimes where the defendant need only intend the prohibited act itself, without intent for a further consequence.
plainEnglish: Intending the act itself, but not necessarily a specific further outcome.

definition: An agreement between two or more persons to commit an unlawful act, typically requiring an overt act in furtherance.
plainEnglish: A plot between two or more people to commit a crime.

definition: An inchoate crime consisting of an intent to commit a specific offense plus a substantial step toward its commission.
plainEnglish: Trying to commit a crime but not actually completing it.

definition: An inchoate crime consisting of asking, encouraging, or commanding another person to commit a crime.
plainEnglish: Asking, encouraging, or hiring someone else to commit a crime.

definition: A person who knowingly assists or encourages another to commit a crime, sharing in the principal's criminal intent.
plainEnglish: Someone who helps another person commit a crime.

definition: A defense justifying otherwise criminal conduct undertaken to prevent a greater imminent harm.
plainEnglish: Breaking the law to prevent a worse harm.

definition: A defense that the defendant was induced by law enforcement to commit a crime they would not otherwise have committed.
plainEnglish: When the police talk you into committing a crime you wouldn't have committed on your own.

definition: A provision in a mortgage or deed of trust authorizing the lender to sell the property upon default without going through judicial foreclosure.
plainEnglish: A clause letting the lender sell the property without going to court if you default.

definition: The legal process by which a lender takes possession of mortgaged property when the borrower defaults on payments.
plainEnglish: The bank taking your house when you stop paying the mortgage.

definition: A deed transferring whatever interest the grantor has in real property, without warranties about the quality of title.
plainEnglish: A deed that transfers whatever ownership the seller has—no guarantees.

definition: A deed in which the grantor guarantees clear title to the property and promises to defend against any claims.
plainEnglish: A deed where the seller guarantees they actually own the property free and clear.

definition: A legal claim or charge on property as security for payment of a debt or performance of an obligation.
plainEnglish: A legal claim against property securing a debt.

definition: A warning or caution; in legal practice, often a formal notice filed to delay or prevent action.
plainEnglish: A warning or qualifier.

definition: A direct legal relationship between parties (e.g., privity of contract), historically required to enforce certain rights or obligations.
plainEnglish: Being in a direct legal relationship with someone (like a direct contract).

definition: A body of law developed to address the rigidity of common law, providing remedies based on fairness; also refers to the value of an ownership interest.
plainEnglish: Fairness-based justice that fills the gaps in strict legal rules; also, the ownership value in an asset.

definition: A non-monetary remedy granted in equity, such as injunctions, specific performance, or rescission, available when legal remedies are inadequate.
plainEnglish: A non-money remedy—like making someone do, or stop doing, something.

definition: An equitable remedy that cancels a contract and restores the parties to their pre-contract positions.
plainEnglish: Undoing a contract and putting everyone back where they started.

definition: An equitable remedy correcting a written contract to reflect the parties' true agreement when the writing contains a mutual mistake or fraud.
plainEnglish: Rewriting a contract to fix what the parties actually agreed to but mistyped.

definition: A remedy returning a party to their original position by requiring the wrongdoer to give back what they unjustly gained.
plainEnglish: Making the wrongdoer give back what they wrongly got.

definition: An equitable doctrine requiring a person who has unfairly benefited at another's expense to return the benefit or its value.
plainEnglish: When someone gets a benefit they shouldn't have kept—the law makes them give it back.

definition: An equitable doctrine allowing recovery of the reasonable value of services provided when no enforceable contract exists.
plainEnglish: 'As much as deserved'—paying someone the fair value of their work even without a formal contract.

definition: An obligation imposed by law to prevent unjust enrichment, even though no actual contract exists between the parties.
plainEnglish: Not a real contract, but the law treats it like one to prevent unfairness.

definition: A written statement of facts sworn to under oath before an authorized officer such as a notary.
plainEnglish: A sworn written statement.

definition: A written statement made under penalty of perjury, similar to an affidavit but not requiring a notary in many jurisdictions.
plainEnglish: A written statement made under penalty of perjury—like an affidavit but no notary required.

definition: The criminal offense of knowingly making a false statement under oath in a judicial proceeding.
plainEnglish: Lying under oath.

definition: Conduct that defies the authority of a court, such as disobeying an order or disrupting proceedings; may be civil or criminal.
plainEnglish: Disobeying or disrespecting the court—you can be jailed or fined for it.

definition: A penalty imposed by a court or other authority for violation of a rule, often in the form of fines, dismissal, or evidentiary preclusion.
plainEnglish: A punishment imposed by the court for misconduct.

definition: A judgment entered against a party who fails to plead or otherwise defend an action.
plainEnglish: Winning automatically because the other side didn't show up or respond.

definition: An agreement between parties to resolve a dispute, typically involving payment and a release of claims, ending the litigation.
plainEnglish: Resolving the case before or during trial with an agreement, usually for money.

definition: A written agreement in which one party gives up a legal claim or right against another.
plainEnglish: A document where you agree to give up your right to sue.

definition: A voluntary, non-binding process in which a neutral third party facilitates negotiations between disputing parties to help them reach a mutually acceptable resolution.
plainEnglish: A neutral helps the parties try to work out a deal—no decision is imposed.

definition: A process where parties submit a dispute to a neutral third party (arbitrator) whose decision is typically binding and enforceable, often pursuant to a contractual arbitration clause.
plainEnglish: A private alternative to court where an arbitrator decides the case—usually binding.

definition: A direct discussion between parties (or their representatives) aimed at reaching agreement, without the involvement of a neutral third party.
plainEnglish: The parties (and their lawyers) just hash it out directly.

definition: A general order issued by a judge or court that applies to all cases or all matters of a certain type before that court, rather than to a specific case.
plainEnglish: A judge's general rules that apply to every case in their court.

definition: A written legal document submitted to a court arguing the law and facts in support of a party's position on a motion, appeal, or other issue.
plainEnglish: A formal written argument submitted to the court.

definition: The court's determination of a matter of law that is necessary to its decision and is binding precedent on later cases.
plainEnglish: The legal rule the court actually decided—the binding part of the opinion.

definition: Statements in a judicial opinion that are not necessary to the decision and therefore not binding as precedent.
plainEnglish: Things a court says in an opinion that aren't the actual rule of the case—not binding.

definition: A prior court decision that serves as authority for deciding later cases involving similar issues.
plainEnglish: An earlier ruling that guides (or binds) future cases on the same issue.

definition: Legal authority that a court is required to follow, such as decisions of higher courts in the same jurisdiction.
plainEnglish: Law a court has to follow.

definition: Legal authority that a court may consider but is not required to follow, such as decisions from other jurisdictions or law review articles.
plainEnglish: Law a court can consider but isn't required to follow.

definition: A separate opinion by a judge agreeing with the result of the majority but offering different or additional reasoning.
plainEnglish: A judge who agrees with the outcome but for different reasons.

definition: A separate opinion by a judge disagreeing with the majority's result, reasoning, or both.
plainEnglish: A judge's opinion saying the majority got it wrong.

definition: A formal written statement filed with the court setting forth a party's claims or defenses, such as a complaint, answer, or reply.
plainEnglish: The formal documents that set out each side's claims and defenses.

definition: The Fifth Amendment right not to be compelled to testify against oneself in a criminal case.
plainEnglish: The right to 'plead the Fifth' and refuse to answer questions that could incriminate you.

definition: The Sixth Amendment right of a criminal defendant to be represented by an attorney at critical stages of the prosecution, including at trial.
plainEnglish: The right to a lawyer in criminal cases (and to a free one if you can't afford it).

definition: A civil claim seeking damages for a wrongful act causing harm, distinct from a claim for breach of contract.
plainEnglish: A lawsuit over a wrongful act causing injury (not a contract violation).

definition: The legal basis for a lawsuit—the facts and legal theory that entitle a plaintiff to a remedy from a defendant.
plainEnglish: The legal reason for the lawsuit—the theory and facts that justify suing.

definition: Formal information given to a party about a legal proceeding or matter affecting their rights, required by due process before adverse action.
plainEnglish: Officially telling someone about a legal matter that affects them.

definition: Notice imputed by law to a person based on information that could have been discovered through reasonable inquiry, such as recorded documents.
plainEnglish: Notice you're treated as having even if you didn't actually know, because the information was publicly available.

definition: A legal fiction representing an ordinarily prudent person, used as the objective standard for evaluating conduct, especially in negligence cases.
plainEnglish: The hypothetical 'average careful person' the law compares your behavior to.

definition: Whether a reasonable person could have anticipated the harm that resulted from their conduct; central to duty and proximate cause analysis.
plainEnglish: Whether a reasonable person could have seen the harm coming.

definition: A lawsuit lacking any legal merit or factual basis, often filed for improper purposes and subject to sanctions.
plainEnglish: A lawsuit with no real legal basis—the kind that can get the filer sanctioned.

definition: A tort claim against someone who initiated a baseless legal action with malice and without probable cause, where the prior action terminated in the plaintiff's favor.
plainEnglish: Suing someone for suing you in bad faith with no legal basis.

definition: A tort consisting of using a legal process primarily for an ulterior purpose not intended by the law, even if the process itself was originally proper.
plainEnglish: Misusing a legal procedure (even a legitimate one) for an improper purpose.

definition: The wrongful exercise of control over another's personal property to the extent that justifies forcing payment of full value.
plainEnglish: Treating someone else's property as your own—the civil version of theft.

definition: An unlawful intrusion that interferes with another's right to possession of property, whether to land (trespass to land) or personal property (trespass to chattels).
plainEnglish: Entering or interfering with someone else's property without permission.

definition: A tort involving substantial and unreasonable interference with the use and enjoyment of land (private nuisance) or with a public right (public nuisance).
plainEnglish: Substantially interfering with someone's use of their property (private) or with public rights (public).

definition: An intentional misrepresentation of a material fact, made with knowledge of falsity and intent to induce reliance, causing damages.
plainEnglish: Intentionally lying to trick someone into doing something that harms them.

definition: A false statement of material fact made by one party that another reasonably relies on to their detriment; may be innocent, negligent, or fraudulent.
plainEnglish: A false statement someone reasonably believed and acted on, to their detriment.

definition: Knowledge of wrongdoing or falsity, particularly in fraud cases; an element requiring proof that the defendant knew of the falsity or acted with reckless disregard.
plainEnglish: 'Knowingly'—the requirement that the defendant knew what they were doing was wrong or false.

definition: The act of depending on a representation or promise, often a required element in claims of fraud, misrepresentation, and promissory estoppel.
plainEnglish: Acting based on what someone said or promised.

definition: Honesty in fact and the observance of reasonable commercial standards of fair dealing, often an implied duty in contractual performance.
plainEnglish: Acting honestly and fairly.
related: duty of good faith and fair dealing

definition: Dishonest or unfair conduct, especially the deliberate breach of the duty of good faith and fair dealing in contracts.
plainEnglish: Acting dishonestly or unfairly, often deliberately.

definition: A doubt based on reason and common sense after consideration of all the evidence; the level of doubt that prevents conviction in a criminal case.
plainEnglish: A real, common-sense doubt—the kind that means a jury can't convict.

definition: A person who commits a tort and is therefore liable to the injured party.
plainEnglish: Someone who commits a tort.

definition: One of two or more persons whose combined wrongful acts caused a single injury, potentially leading to joint and several liability.
plainEnglish: One of multiple wrongdoers whose acts combined to cause a single injury.

definition: A statutory cause of action allowing survivors to sue for damages when a person's death is caused by another's wrongful or negligent act.
plainEnglish: Suing because someone's wrongful act caused a death.

definition: A cause of action that survives the death of the injured party, allowing the estate to recover damages the deceased could have claimed if they had lived.
plainEnglish: Damages the dead person could have claimed if they'd lived—pursued by the estate.

definition: About to occur immediately; required for several legal concepts such as assault and self-defense.
plainEnglish: Right about to happen.

definition: The factual link between conduct and harm, typically shown by the but-for test or, in some cases, the substantial factor test.
plainEnglish: The factual showing that the defendant's act actually caused the harm.

definition: An equitable remedy requiring a party to perform the exact obligations specified in a contract, granted when monetary damages would be inadequate.
plainEnglish: The court orders someone to actually do what they promised, not just pay money.

definition: A legal procedure by which a creditor obtains payment of a debt directly from a third party (such as the debtor's employer or bank) who owes money to the debtor.
plainEnglish: Pulling money out of someone's wages or bank account to pay a judgment.

definition: A notice filed in public records warning that title to a specific property is the subject of pending litigation.
plainEnglish: A public notice that a property is tied up in a lawsuit.

definition: Title to real property free from reasonable doubt or defect, such that a prudent buyer would accept it; a common requirement in real estate contracts.
plainEnglish: Title clean enough that a reasonable buyer would accept it.

definition: A doctrine preventing a party from asserting a claim or defense inconsistent with their prior conduct, representations, or judicial findings.
plainEnglish: Being barred from making an argument because of something you said or did earlier.
